text:
marta: Noticing sustained NVMe write-amplification on eu-west3 hosts after the nightly compaction window. IOPS are OK but write throughput and latency spike, and several GPU attach operations time out.

kevin: dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/NVME/write-amplification?orgId=1 - widening the view now. :mag_right:

marta: Short log extract from node euw3-gnode-211:
```
[ 20945.7123] nvme nvme1: write amplification ratio=4.8, avg latency=6.2ms, p99=45ms
[ 20946.0010] kernel: nvme_core: controller slowing I/O due to write-back pressure
[ 20946.3501] kubelet: attach timeout for pod job-ml-77 (attach timed out)
```

jasmin: kernel + fw? any recent changes in eu-west3?

marta: kernel=6.3.8, nvme-fw=ZX-2.1. Firmware rolled in two weeks ago across EU regions, but only eu-west3 coincides with new compaction timing (we bumped compaction concurrency to speed GC).

kevin: can we correlate with compactor job starts? marta, can you run `grep compactor /var/log/compaction.log | tail -n 50` and paste results?

marta: pasted last 50 lines to the incident board. Quick snippet:
```
2026-03-21T01:00:03Z compactor[euw3-shard-4]: start compaction cycles=8 concurrency=6
2026-03-21T01:03:12Z compactor[euw3-shard-4]: checkpoint write delta=120GB
```

kevin: that's it. Concurrency=6 + full checkpoint writes = sustained write bursts. On these flash arrays that increases internal garbage collection -> write amplification.

jasmin: short-term: 1) reduce compaction concurrency in eu-west3 to 1, 2) add a scrub/compaction avoid-window overlapping peak provision times (02:30-04:30 UTC), 3) taint the hottest nodes so new GPU pods don't land there. I can push compactor config patch.

marta: applying taint now:
```
kubectl taint nodes euw3-gnode-2{08..18} ephemeral-nvme-wam=true:NoSchedule
```

ops-bot: [deploy] compactor-config v4.12.0 -> v4.12.1: concurrency cap for eu-west3 set to 1, avoid-window added (02:30-04:30 UTC). Rollout started.

kevin: medium-term: schedule compactions during lower provisioning windows, or stagger checkpoint writes to avoid concurrent large flushes. Also request vendor support to review FW GC aggressiveness.

marta: opened vendor ticket NVME-5679 with vendor-pm, attaching nvme-cli SMART data and `iostat -x 1 15` outputs. s3://redwood-artifacts/infra/nvme-wam/3312000000.tar.gz

jasmin: also enabling attach circuit-breaker for provisioner so after X attach failures host is quarantined for 10m. Patch to node-provisioner queued.

kevin: we should also consider routing critical GPU workloads to eu-west1 for next 2 hours to avoid customer impact. Cost vs latency decision: ops keeps critical-only.

marta: live migration scheduled for 45m window. Starting canary: moving 3 critical pods to eu-west1 now.

oncall: pinged. I'll monitor node failures and escalate if any node becomes read-only.

kevin: INC-2026-3319 created. Actions: compactor concurrency rollback, taint hot nodes, enable circuit-breaker, vendor ticket NVME-5679, migrate critical workloads. Update in 15m. :timer_clock:

marta: note for postmortem: avoid increasing compaction concurrency in regions with older NVMe FW + small fans; document compaction vs scrub collision.

jasmin: agreed. Adding runbook step to check `nvme-cli smart-log` for write amplification signals before bumping compaction.

marta: thanks all — will post artifacts and follow vendor replies in this thread.

ops-bot: [artifact] uploaded nvme-wam/3312000000.tar.gz (3.4MB) to s3.

kevin: update at +15m or sooner if anything flips. :thumbsup:
